title: KDgate for Montreal mayor continues with website mocking Kraft Dinner comments
summary: Controversy in a box: Montreal Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada’s Kraft Dinner comments spark website, impromptu protest at city hall.

image.caption: Boxes of Kraft Dinner were already visible near city hall on Thursday morning. (Simon-Marc Charron/Radio-Canada)

blocks.text: Montreal·Updated
Controversy in a box: Montreal Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada’s Kraft Dinner comments spark website, impromptu protest at city hall.
Soraya Martinez Ferrada acknowledged comment was awkward, but backlash continues
The controversy over her Kraft Dinner comments is sticking to Montreal Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada.
The City of Montreal unveiled a budget that featured a property tax average increase of 9.8 per cent — about three times the inflation rate – on Tuesday.
The budget is due to be adopted in mid-December.
But an ill-timed Kraft Dinner comparison over budget choices has been haunting the mayor, giving rise to a website created by a Montreal software developer presenting the city budget on KD boxes.
There is also a protest outside city hall later Thursday afternoon.
The landing page for the website, kdgate.ca, alludes to the mayor's comments. (Submitted by kdgate.ca)

Martinez Ferrada’s comments during an interview with French-language media outlet Quartre95, a personal finance site, following the budget rollout compared creating a municipal budget to decisions taken at home.
"We're going through every service to see what we can save. It's like when you make your personal budget: if you know you'll have less money one year, then, you have to make choices," she said.
"Sometimes, you'll have to eat a little more Kraft Dinner because you can't afford filet mignon."
The comments were walked back by Martinez Ferrada on Wednesday morning in an Instagram story where she described the comparison as “clumsy.”
"What I meant was that when we make choices, the city is the same as when we make personal choices," she said.
The website, kdgate.ca, includes a rundown of the city budget listed in a way that mirrors the nutritional facts on the back of a food item. (Submitted by kdgate.ca)
But not before it unleashed a torrent of backlash on social media, framing her remarks as out of touch with the reality of Montrealers dealing with higher cost-of-living.
On Thursday morning, a website, kdgate.ca, was published outlining a municipal budget in the form of nutritional information on the packaging of the popular comfort food.

blocks.text: Niko Draca, the Montrealer behind the site, told CBC News about what prompted him to create the site.
"I saw a lot of outrage over the comment and I wanted to turn it into something positive and really get people looking at this data," Draca said.
"These documents are usually quite long and dry, so I figured a fun way to visualize could help, basically using the KD comment as a hook."
Meanwhile, a “Soraya Dinner” is planned for Thursday afternoon in front of Montreal’s city hall.
Organizers are inviting demonstrators to bring a pot, a portable stove and their own ingredients.
